source: A credentialed cross-origin POST from a same-scheme, same-site sibling origin to the victim tenant mark-read route.
control: Customer session and current-thread authorization apply, and the cookie is SameSite=Lax, but the available assertAllowedTenantOrigin control is not invoked; proof that an attacker controls a script-capable same-site sibling in a real deployment is missing.
sink: markCurrentUserThreadRead resolves the victim's authorized thread and calls Chatwoot updatePublicConversationLastSeen.
impact: If the sibling-origin precondition holds, an attacker can change one victim thread's Chatwoot last-seen/read-state integrity; no cross-tenant read, admin action, or high-impact effect was proved.
preconditions: Victim has an active customer session and ready thread; attacker can execute script on a same-scheme sibling origin within the victim host's registrable site; credentialed fetch sends the host cookie. The immutable repository does not establish that attacker-origin fact for a real deployment.

evidence.result: The route omits the existing exact tenant-Origin validator and reaches the Chatwoot last-seen write after normal customer/thread checks on both byte-identical baselines.
The shipped portal does not prove arbitrary tenant JavaScript hosting, and custom tenant domains need not be same-site; SameSite=Lax defeats ordinary cross-site cookie attachment.
Need a real deployment domain-ownership inventory or browser test proving an attacker-controlled script-capable sibling origin in the actual provider/custom-domain topology.

source: An in-scope compromised or misconfigured TLS-terminating upstream replays one observed valid signed webhook within five minutes while varying the unsigned x-chatwoot-delivery header.
control: The HMAC verifies timestamp plus raw body and tenant/account/inbox invariants, but it does not bind the delivery header that is preferred as the dedupe key.
sink: Tenant plus delivery_key uniqueness accepts every changed header as new, persists a row, then runs realtime snapshot and message-created push effects.
impact: Unbounded changed keys within the signature window repeat notification/realtime work and database writes for one tenant and can pressure shared backend and provider capacity.
preconditions: Observe one raw body, timestamp, and signature at a trusted upstream or TLS terminator; replay before the five-minute tolerance expires; preserve signed bytes while changing only the delivery header. This is not an ordinary unauthenticated internet path.

evidence.result: Exact source/control/sink trace shows the unsigned header becomes the only tenant-scoped uniqueness key before realtime/push effects on both unchanged baselines.
A fixed synthetic signature verified both before and after changing only x-chatwoot-delivery: baseVerified=true, changedDeliveryVerified=true, sameSignature=true.
TLS, body HMAC, tenant invariants, and five-minute tolerance exclude ordinary remote forgery and lower likelihood; they do not bind or cap the changed key.

source: A previously legitimate tenant administrator retains an unexpired portal admin cookie after Chatwoot disables, unconfirms, removes, or demotes the agent.
control: Current-session resolution checks only tenant, token hash, and expiresAt, touches lastSeenAt, and trusts the persisted administrator snapshot; live Chatwoot eligibility is used only during challenge creation.
sink: The common admin guard authorizes branding, legal-document, and integration-admin reads and mutations with the stale portal session.
impact: Current upstream revocation does not stop same-tenant portal administrator actions for up to the fixed 12-hour portal-session lifetime.
preconditions: Attacker was legitimately authorized and logged in before revocation, retains the cookie, and acts before portal logout, session-row deletion, or expiry; no cross-tenant use is required or proved.

evidence.result: Live eligibility and active-session resolution are disjoint; protected routes rely on the stale snapshot on both byte-identical baselines.
Ordinary admin request/verify/session integration behavior passed, confirming the persisted session is the protected-route authority; no adversarial revocation assertion exists.
Tenant binding, exact Origin on mutations, explicit logout, initial live verification, and 12-hour expiry bound scope and duration but do not implement upstream revocation.

source: Authorized read and typing successes create distinct process-global tenant/user/thread throttle keys over a long-lived multi-tenant runtime.
control: Read and typing-on throttle windows overwrite repeated keys, but no TTL or size eviction exists; typing deletes only after a successful off for the exact key and each replica has separate state.
sink: The two Maps allocated in app startup retain successful read keys indefinitely and typing keys until explicit successful off or process restart.
impact: Gradual process-memory cardinality growth and cross-replica throttle inconsistency as tenants, users, threads, churn, and runtime lifetime grow.
preconditions: Many authorized user/thread combinations or long-running churn; a single user has bounded valid threads, repeats overwrite, and process restart clears state.

evidence.result: Read keys have no delete path and typing keys rely on later successful off; both Maps live for the app process on unchanged baselines.
Presence tests passed and confirm shared stores across request-scoped services, repeated-key throttling, and typing-off deletion.
F-LOAD-006 records the identical source/control/sink/impact and its TTL/size-bounded eviction plus replica decision closes the complete tuple.

source: An unauthenticated remote caller submits candidate email addresses to the tenant-admin challenge request route.
control: Exact Origin and a five-per-minute per-process tenant/IP limiter apply, but live eligibility is exposed through eligible success versus an explicit 403 TENANT_ADMIN_NOT_ELIGIBLE response.
sink: The public response reveals whether the address is a confirmed administrator in the tenant Chatwoot account and sends a challenge only for eligible users.
impact: Tenant administrator membership/role enumeration that assists targeting; no code, session, or protected data is issued to ineligible callers.
preconditions: Know the tenant host and candidate addresses and issue direct same-Origin-header requests within or distributed around the process-local IP limit.

evidence.result: The public service performs live administrator verification and maps ineligible results to a distinct 403 on both unchanged baselines.
Targeted admin integration checks reproduced eligible challenge success and ineligible explicit 403 with no email sent.
F-AUTH-002 records the same oracle and requires indistinguishable public semantics while preserving internal delivery/audit outcomes, closing the complete tuple.

source: One authenticated customer issues repeated or concurrent same-origin multipart avatar uploads, each up to 15 MiB.
control: Session, exact Origin, one-file/part limits, a 15 MiB body/file cap, claimed MIME allowlist, and Chatwoot timeout bound one request; no user, tenant, request-rate, aggregate-byte, or concurrency admission control exists.
sink: The route fully buffers the part, the service copies/normalizes it, and the backend synchronously PUTs multipart bytes to the linked Chatwoot contact using the tenant API credential.
impact: Ten concurrent max-size requests hold at least 150 MiB of attacker bytes and make ten upstream writes; 100 hold at least 1.5 GiB before runtime/FormData overhead and make 100 writes, plausibly exhausting the shared process or Chatwoot capacity.
preconditions: Valid customer session, linked Chatwoot contact, same-origin request context, and bandwidth/concurrency sufficient to upload repeated accepted bodies; actual container memory/provider thresholds are unavailable.

evidence.result: Exact route/service/client trace proves full buffering and one authenticated Chatwoot PUT per accepted request with no route-specific or aggregate admission control on both baselines.
Profile route tests passed, including a positive multipart upload reaching updateCurrentUserAvatar and individual request-shape rejection controls.
Authentication, Origin, per-request byte/part/MIME limits, and upstream deadlines reduce reach and bound one request but do not bound concurrent aggregate memory or writes.

source: An authenticated customer concurrently sends or triggers recovery against one not-yet-bootstrapped or stale thread.
control: A transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock serializes the tenant/contact key, but each waiter holds a pool transaction connection and the handler uses outer-db repository calls and awaits Chatwoot before releasing the transaction.
sink: Same-key waiters and the lock holder occupy the shared bounded node-postgres pool across global DB acquisition and Chatwoot source/conversation creation.
impact: Connection convoy or pool exhaustion can delay unrelated requests and tenants; enough waiters can prevent the lock holder's outer-db work from obtaining a connection.
preconditions: Cold or stale conversation mapping, concurrent authorized requests on the same key, and enough requests to approach pool capacity; established threads bypass bootstrap and text sends are limited to 20 per minute per user/thread.

evidence.result: The transaction holds pg_advisory_xact_lock while handler repository operations use the outer db and Chatwoot calls are awaited on both unchanged baselines.
Targeted chat-thread service tests passed ordinary bootstrap/recovery behavior; the repository test only proves lock execution and does not falsify pool convoy.
F-LOAD-002 records the identical cold/recovery source, transaction/advisory control, external-I/O/pool sink and convoy impact; its durable short-transaction claim remedy closes the tuple.

source: Unauthenticated callers repeat password, passwordless, reset, setup, and tenant-admin authentication requests through a deployment with more than one backend process.
control: registerAuthRateLimit creates one in-process Map keyed by route group, tenant/host, and request IP; there is no shared atomic replica counter.
sink: Each replica admits its own full allowance before password/hash, database, email, Chatwoot lookup, or code-verification work.
impact: Intended request budgets multiply by backend replica count, increasing guessing and resource/email work; the recovered evidence does not establish a distinct successful account takeover.
preconditions: Multiple backend processes and routing that lets a caller reach them. Actual replica/shared-ingress policy is unavailable and reference Compose declares one backend service, so historical runtime reachability is unclear.

evidence.result: Limiter state is unambiguously local to one Fastify process on both byte-identical baselines.
Targeted app tests reproduced five allowed attempts and a sixth 429 inside one app instance; they provide no cross-instance sharing evidence.
F-AUTH-001 records the same replica-bypass tuple and requires shared counters before multi-instance deployment; the reference Compose single service makes actual reachability deployment-dependent.

source: An authenticated current thread participant repeatedly chooses search queries/cursors that scan older history, with worst-case existing pages containing unique missing reply targets.
control: Current-thread authority, query length, 8 scanned pages, 20 results, and request timeouts bound one call, but search has no route-specific rate, external-call, concurrency, coalescing, or aggregate budget.
sink: Each page calls Chatwoot listConversationMessages and Promise.all resolves every unique missing reply target; the concrete client adds cursor-anchor and older-page history probes.
impact: One search can drive up to 23 base history HTTP calls plus 160 reply-target calls, 183 total; 10 or 100 concurrent searches can request up to 1,830 or 18,300 upstream calls and degrade shared portal/Chatwoot availability.
preconditions: Valid customer session and current thread membership; ready conversation with enough history; worst reply fan-out requires 20 unique missing reply targets per page, while the 23-call base path needs only eight older pages; caller controls repetition and concurrency.

evidence.result: Exact route/service/mapper/client trace proves bounded-but-high per-request history probes and no aggregate admission control on both unchanged baselines.
Synthetic service invocation returned listCalls=8 and replyCalls=160 for eight 20-message pages; targeted search tests also passed ordinary behavior.
Finite page/result caps, current-thread authority, and timeouts constrain one request and errors; they do not reduce the 183-call maximum or bound concurrent requests.
